value.expectation_copy: Verbatim UI copy that labels the try-on as real vs approximation: "Virtual try-on gives you a quick way to preview styles before you buy." and "Treat it as a helpful visual guide."
value.gap_vs_onpoint: Gaps relative to OnPoint: Walmart Be Your Own Model is SKU-specific and uses a proxy-model visualization; it does not expose a SKU-to-model-accurate fit graph or a universally accessible agent/buyer checkout surface. Walmart’s pathway relies on first-party catalog/stock data and a visually guided experience labeled as a visual aid rather than a guaranteed fit, with a dense mass-retailer UX that can bury the try-on CTA for non-eligible SKUs. OnPoint could outperform by delivering a true, supply-graph-backed, locally-pay-enabled agent purchase flow that uses a transparent fit model with explicit sizing, stock-location metadata, and ready-made proxies (or privacy-preserving personal-model uploads) that integrate with WhatsApp/M-Pesa in target markets; plus a public API for quote/reserve/pay that aligns with local currencies and payment rails.
value.pricing_tiers: Free to use for try-on; no tiered pricing observed; Walmart+ upsell unrelated to try-on access.

value.value_proposition: Walmart Be Your Own Model offers a SKU-specific virtual try-on using a proxy-model (no personal photo required) that renders the exact eligible garment on a model for free; it is framed as a visual guide rather than a guarantee of fit.
value.what_onpoint_should_copy: Adopt Walmart’s pattern of placing a clear Try-On CTA on the product image for eligible SKUs, enable a proxy-model flow with provided size/height data, and label the experience as a free, visual guide rather than a guaranteed fit. Additionally, expose model metadata alongside SKU to improve perceived fidelity, and pursue local-pay handoffs (e.g., WhatsApp/M-Pesa) and explicit inventory/stock visibility to empower agent purchases.
